allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A retelling of Dragon Ball's origin with a different take on the meeting of Goku, Bulma, and Kame-Sen'nin. It also retells the Red Ribbon Army story; but this time they find Goku rather than Goku finding them.

facts.overview: A retelling of Dragon Ball's origin with a different take on the meeting of Goku, Bulma, and Kame-Sen'nin. It also retells the Red Ribbon Army story; but this time they find Goku rather than Goku finding them.
facts.title: Dragon Ball: The Path to Power

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: With the Red Ribbon Army actively hunting Goku from the start, how will these newly formed alliances withstand being tracked down so early?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: In this retold origin, Goku crosses paths with Bulma and Kame-Sen'nin under new circumstances, quickly drawing the attention of the Red Ribbon Army, who actively hunt him down instead of waiting to be found.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Fast-moving fantasy adventure, moderate stakes, and vibrant animated excitement built for engaged group viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Shigeyasu Yamauchi, this brisk 80-minute animated fantasy flips the classic pursuit dynamic into a fast-paced, exciting collision with an encroaching army.

claudeAdvisory.claimSpan: actively hunt him down instead of waiting to be found
issueSummaries: description says the Red Ribbon Army 'actively hunt him down' after 'quickly drawing the attention' of the Army. The overview says only that 'they find Goku rather than Goku finding them'. 'Find' is turned into an active hunt, and the quick, attention-drawing sequence is not stated. 'Instead of waiting to be found' also garbles the inversion, because the overview inverts who does the finding and says nothing about the Army 'waiting'. These are unsupported causal and mechanistic concretizations.

curiosityHook adds timing and relationship claims the packet does not state: the Army is 'actively hunting Goku from the start', the heroes are 'newly formed alliances', and they are 'tracked down so early'. The overview names only a different take on the meeting of Goku, Bulma and Kame-Sen'nin and the Army finding Goku. It gives no alliance, no 'from the start' or 'so early' timing, and no pursuit.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: The core premise (retold Dragon Ball origin, a new take on the meeting of Goku, Bulma and Kame-Sen'nin, the Red Ribbon Army finding Goku instead of the reverse, the director, the runtime, the genres) is grounded, and vibeSummary and whyWatch are within tolerance as genre shorthand. In description and curiosityHook, however, the plain 'they find Goku' is escalated into an active hunt with a fast sequence ('quickly', 'from the start', 'so early') and a specified relationship ('newly formed alliances'). Together these falsely specify plot mechanics, timing and relationships, which are named materiality categories under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1, and they shape viewer expectations of the film's structure. They do not contradict the source, reveal an outcome or ending, or invent identities, so the severity is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would stay with 'the Red Ribbon Army find Goku instead of Goku finding them' and drop the hunt, the alliance, and the 'from the start' and 'so early' timing.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: the retold origin, the different take on the meeting of Goku, Bulma and Kame-Sen'nin ('under new circumstances'), and the Red Ribbon Army retelling in which they find Goku all restate the overview. The character names match.

description: 'actively hunt him down', 'quickly drawing the attention' and 'instead of waiting to be found' have no basis in the overview. The overview says the Army finds Goku, and it does not say they hunt him, that his meeting the other two draws their attention, or that this happens quickly. The overview inverts who finds whom and does not describe the Army as waiting.

curiosityHook: 'from the start', 'so early', 'newly formed alliances' and 'tracked down' are not stated. The packet supports a meeting and an Army that finds Goku. The alliance framing specifies a relationship, and the timing words specify story sequence.

whyWatch: 'animated fantasy' matches genres Animation/Fantasy, and 'Shigeyasu Yamauchi' and '80-minute' match director and runtimeMinutes. 'Flips the classic pursuit dynamic' echoes the overview's 'rather than Goku finding them'. 'Classic' and 'pursuit' are mild framing and are treated as tolerated, although 'classic' leans on franchise history the packet only implies. 'Encroaching army' is figurative shorthand for the Army finding Goku.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Fast-moving' and 'brisk' match pace=fast. 'Exciting' matches mood exciting. 'Moderate stakes' matches emotionalWeight=moderate. 'Engaged group viewing' matches attentionDemand=engaged and situations=[friends, family]. Keyword-only material (android, resurrection, martial arts) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. Because the overview says the Army finds Goku, an adjudicator could read 'hunt him down' as harmless urgency and approve the description. The curiosityHook's 'alliances' and 'from the start' would then be the closest calls. I flag both fields because the same escalation recurs in two places and several small unsupported specifics accumulate. The phrase 'instead of waiting to be found' is also garbled against the overview's inversion, so it may need rewording even if the hunt framing is accepted. 'Under new circumstances' and 'flips the classic pursuit dynamic' were considered and left within tolerance. Reviewing this packet closed-world, I have no external knowledge of the franchise to check the 'classic' framing against.

Phrasing such as 'newly formed alliances' and 'encroaching army' functions as acceptable narrative shorthand and thematic framing without importing ungrounded Dragon Ball franchise lore, external characters, or spoiler-boundary breaches. The experiential descriptors in whyWatch and vibeSummary map cleanly to verified metadata and authorized semantic tags.
